procedural_matters: SUI 1886 was represented by Olivier Marchand.
FRA 297 was represented by Erwan Vannier.
Robert Hartmann (skipper of SUI 1886) and Walter Saettone (jib trimmer of FRA 297) attended the hearing as observers.
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 11 knots of wind and choppy waves.
SUI 1886 was approaching the windward mark on the second beat on a closed-hauled course on starboard tack.
FRA 297 was approaching on port tack on a closed-hauled course, on a converging course with SUI 1886.
While SUI 1886 was entering the zone and when the boats were approximately 4 meters apart, FRA 297 luffed.
Immediately after, there was contact between the bow of FRA 297 and the last quarter of the port side of SUI 1886.
There was a hole of about 10 cm in diameter at 20 cm from the stern of the port side of SUI 1886. There was a possibility for water to get in.
There was gelcoat damage on FRA 297, 10 cm down from the bow.
FRA 297 took a Two-Turns Penalty after the offset mark.
conclusions: FRA 297 on port tack failed to keep clear of SUI 1886 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
FRA 297 did not avoid contact with SUI 1886 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for SUI 1886, the right-of-way boat, to avoid contact with FRA 297 when it became clear that FRA 297 was not keeping clear. SUI 1886 did not break RRS 14(a).
Since FRA 297 caused serious damage by her breach, her penalty was to retire as required by RRS 44.1(b).
